tool.name: DIA-NN In Silico Library Generation
tool.description: Generate in silico predicted spectral library using DIA-NN deep learning predictor. This module uses DIA-NN software for data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics data processing. Output materials should include attribution: "Generated using DIA-NN".
tool.command: diann --fasta '$fasta_input' --fasta-search --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --predictor --gen-spec-lib #if $advanced.missed_cleavages --missed-cleavages $advanced.missed_cleavages #end if #if $advanced.min_pep_length --min-pep-len $advanced.min_pep_length #end if #if $advanced.max_pep_length --max-pep-len $advanced.max_pep_length #end if #if $advanced.min_charge --min-charge $advanced.min_charge #end if #if $advanced.max_charge --max-charge $advanced.max_charge #end if #if $advanced.extra_args $advanced.extra_args #end if && cp *lib.log.txt output.log

param.name: fasta_input
param.label: FASTA Protein Database
param.help: Protein sequence database in FASTA format for spectral library prediction

param.name: missed_cleavages
param.label: Missed Cleavages
param.help: Maximum number of missed cleavages allowed (default: 1)

param.name: min_pep_length
param.label: Minimum Peptide Length
param.help: Minimum peptide length for library generation (default: 7)

param.name: max_pep_length
param.label: Maximum Peptide Length
param.help: Maximum peptide length for library generation (default: 30)

tool.help:
**What it does**
DIA-NN In Silico Library Generation uses deep learning to generate predicted spectral libraries from FASTA protein databases. This tool is essential for Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA) proteomics workflows.
The spectral library can then be used with DIA-NN's main analysis tool to identify and quantify peptides in DIA mass spectrometry data.
**Inputs**
- **FASTA Protein Database**: A protein sequence database in FASTA format. This can be a complete proteome or a subset of proteins of interest.
**Advanced Options**
- **Missed Cleavages**: Number of missed tryptic cleavages to consider (default: 1) - **Peptide Length**: Min/max peptide length for library generation (default: 7-30) - **Charge States**: Min/max precursor charge states to predict (default: 1-4)
**Outputs**
- **Predicted Spectral Library**: In silico predicted spectral library (.predicted.speclib format) - **Log**: DIA-NN processing log with statistics and warnings
**How to Use**
1. Upload or select a FASTA protein database 2. Adjust advanced parameters if needed (default values work well for most cases) 3. Run the tool to generate the spectral library 4. Use the output library with DIA-NN analysis tool
**Performance Notes**
- Processing time depends on database size (typically 5-30 minutes for human proteome) - Requires at least 4GB RAM, 8GB+ recommended for large databases - Uses deep learning prediction, so more CPU cores = faster processing
**Citation**
If you use this tool, please cite:
Demichev V, Messner CB, Vernardis SI, Lilley KS, Ralser M. DIA-NN: neural networks and interference correction enable deep proteome coverage in high throughput. Nat Methods. 2020 Jan;17(1):41-44. doi: 10.1038/s41592-020-01009-0
Output materials should include attribution: "Generated using DIA-NN"
**More Information**
- DIA-NN Homepage: https://github.com/vdemichev/DiaNN - Documentation: https://github.com/vdemichev/DiaNN
